title: The Confidence Trap: Calibration Attacks for Graph Neural Networks

problem.claim: The robustness of calibrated graph neural networks to adversarial structural perturbations is insufficiently understood for safety-critical decision-making.

gap.claim: Existing calibration attacks face challenges from discrete graph structures, inadequate underconfidence objectives, and edge perturbations that can cause unintended label changes.

contributions.claim: A Unified Graph Calibration Attack framework is proposed for worst-case white-box analysis of GNN calibration robustness.
The framework combines a KL-divergence loss, reranking, a hybrid loss, and beam search to encourage uniform predictions, reduce or recover from label flips, and broaden adversarial search.
The paper provides theoretical insights linking model generalization, dataset complexity, and calibration vulnerability.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that models with higher accuracy or models trained on datasets with more classes are more susceptible under the stated threat model.
The authors report that extensive experiments show UGCA substantially increases Expected Calibration Error while preserving classification accuracy.
The authors report that their code is publicly available on GitHub.

narrative_sequence.summary: Trustworthy decision-making requires confidence calibration, but calibrated GNNs may be vulnerable to adversarial structural perturbations.
Graph discreteness, insufficient underconfidence objectives, and label changes caused by edge perturbations complicate calibration attacks.
UGCA is introduced as a unified white-box framework for analyzing GNN calibration robustness.
UGCA uses distribution-shaping, reranking, label-recovery, and beam-search mechanisms to construct calibration attacks.
Theory and experiments connect susceptibility to accuracy and class count, and report increased calibration error with preserved accuracy.

source_observation.claim: Edge perturbations can cause unintended label changes, and the framework includes mechanisms to reduce or recover from such violations.

interpretation.claim: Constrained graph attacks require explicit handling of prediction-preservation constraints.

application.claim: Design graph robustness evaluations with label-preservation checks and recovery mechanisms.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the formal constraint definition or recovery success rate.

unknowns: Attack budgets, datasets, model architectures, and experimental baselines are unspecified.
Theoretical assumptions, formal results, and quantitative calibration changes are unspecified.
The scope and limitations of the reported susceptibility relationships are unspecified.
